heuristics.name: antonym-pole
heuristics.description: Two options are near-opposites; the sentence likely turns on that axis, so pick one pole (usually the less neutral one).

heuristics.name: pair-coherence
heuristics.description: Two-blank items: pick the pair whose two words stand in a natural relation (support or clean contrast).

heuristics.name: repeated-word
heuristics.description: A word appears in two options; the key likely contains it; choose the version whose pair coheres.

heuristics.name: abstract-test-word
heuristics.description: Pick the most abstract, test-typical vocabulary word when the others are concrete, technical or niche.

heuristics.name: evaluative-word
heuristics.description: Pick the option with the strongest evaluative sense about a person or behavior.

heuristics.name: odd-one-out
heuristics.description: Pick the option that differs in valence/register from the other three.

notes: reject_certain set false on every item: without the sentence no single option could be ruled out with certainty. Heuristic signals are weak; many signal picks are close to guesses.
